clue.text: One splits Conservative ministers

indicators.note: the word one cuts the Conservative abbreviation open, sitting between its first letter and the rest

parts.note: Cons is a short form for Conservative, as in Con or Cons in party listings
an is the indefinite article, a word meaning one

explanation.surface: A single figure causes a rift among a Tory government's ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Canons are clergy attached to a cathedral, so they are ministers of the church.

clue.text: Bank stopping competition to make big profits

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside a bottle neck, so the bank word is placed inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a competition, such as the FA Cup
to bank is to tilt or lean, as an aircraft does in a turn

explanation.surface: A financial institution halting a contest so as to rake in huge profits.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is an idiom for making a great deal of money, especially quickly.

clue.text: "No to Independence" group nearly clash

parts.note: I is an abbreviation for independence or independent

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is left off the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A No campaign slogan against independence, with the opposing groups almost coming to blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash is a loud jarring sound, so it is a kind of din.

clue.text: Average odds to keep North Sea gas supply

indicators.note: supply read as an adverb, supplely, means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order
the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word keep are taken

explanation.surface: Mediocre chances of maintaining Britain's offshore gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, but read as supple-ly it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something unremarkable or mediocre, so ordinary or average.

clue.text: Disregard fantastic region …

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and unreal, so the letters of region are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay no attention to some fanciful territory, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to pay no attention to something deliberately; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Careless, entertained by happy host

indicators.note: a guest is entertained by a host, so the careless word sits inside the happy word

parts.note: gay in its older sense means merry or happy
lax means careless or slack

explanation.surface: A cheerful party host who is a little slapdash with the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like a party host; it means a multitude, a host of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast assemblage of stars, and host means a great multitude.

clue.text: Ones at back after rotten criminals

indicators.note: after places the word for ones at back following the word for rotten

parts.note: food that is rotten has gone off
enders are those at the end or back

explanation.surface: Those at the rear of a queue pursuing some rotten crooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Offenders are people who break the law, so lawbreakers or crooks.

clue.text: Each garment covers large part of body

parts.note: EA is a standard abbreviation for each, as on price labels

indicators.note: the garment covers, that is wraps around, the letter for large

parts.note: a robe is a garment
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Every item of clothing hides a big section of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy lower lobe of the ear is a small part of the human body.

clue.text: In a maddening way, shrewd Brown standing inside

indicators.note: inside places the brown and standing words within the shrewd word

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or shrewd
rust is a reddish-brown colour
a rating is a ranking or standing

explanation.surface: A shrewd Gordon Brown type stands inside, infuriatingly.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY as shrewd is British slang, as in a fly operator.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning annoyingly or exasperatingly, which matches maddening done as a manner.

clue.text: … by disregarding leader over penultimate contest

indicators.note: over signals the remaining letters are turned the other way round
the leading letter of the word for by is dropped

parts.note: by as in multiplication: three by four means three times four

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: ignoring the front-runner of the race before the final.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the clue before but adds nothing to the parse. 'by' becomes TIMES, 'disregarding leader' leaves IMES, and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-final is the round of a competition that comes just before the final one.

clue.text: Former political leader's red flag flying over road

indicators.note: a flag flying flaps about, so the letters of red flag are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A socialist banner fluttering above a street, credited to some past politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges RED FLAG into GERALDF. The 's after leader is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the 38th President of the United States, a former head of state and party leader.

clue.text: Dismiss welcoming news before European expansion

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the word for dismiss holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to axe someone is to sack or dismiss them
news taken as plural new, and N is a common abbreviation for new, so two of them

explanation.surface: An employer sacks staff on hearing reports, ahead of growth in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension built onto a main building, an addition that expands it.

clue.text: See 23
Confusedly articulates odds — bets not strong

parts.note: SP stands for starting price, the odds on a horse when a race begins

indicators.note: F is forte, the musical marking for loud or strong, which is removed

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet, so flutters are bets

explanation.surface: A gambler sorting out odds and stakes, with the bets all modest ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To splutter is to speak in a hurried, confused way, as when flustered or indignant.

clue.text: Hostile unionist and nationalist drink together

parts.note: cordial is a sweet fruit drink

explanation.surface: Political opponents from both sides sharing a drink, yet still at odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly, so its negative describes an unfriendly, hostile manner.

clue.text: No 10 was often on his back in leadership election

definitions.text: No 10 was often on his back

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the phrase leadership election, across the join

explanation.surface: Sounds like a Downing Street prime minister being harried during a party leadership contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 10' suggests Downing Street and politics; it is the shirt number of the Brazilian footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian football great wore the number ten shirt, so that number was usually printed on his back.

clue.text: Old Scot selected, according to reports

indicators.note: reports here means what is heard, so the answer is a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: selected means picked, chosen

explanation.surface: A historic Scotsman chosen for something, as the stories go.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were an ancient people of northern and eastern Scotland, so one is an early Scotsman.

clue.text: One of two in lead — one's used to season?

indicators.note: in places the one-of-two word inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
of a pair, one is this and the other is the other

explanation.surface: A partner leading the way in a pair, wondering about the time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' hints at a time of year; it means flavouring food.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is a plant grown to flavour cooking, a seasoning herb.

clue.text: Joins in, taking time for craft

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the word for joins contains the time letter

parts.note: seams are the lines where pieces of fabric are joined
in means fashionable, as does hip

explanation.surface: Someone joining in an activity, given enough time, for a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a vessel, and craft is a general word for boats and ships.

clue.text: Need muscles for this reason? Top's removed

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles

indicators.note: the top, first letter of the word for this reason, is taken off

parts.note: hence means therefore, for this reason

explanation.surface: A gym-goer wondering if a bare chest is the excuse for building muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: An absence of something is a lack or want of it, so need in the sense of lack.

clue.text: Country secure following anger

indicators.note: following places the secure word after the anger word

parts.note: ire is anger
to land a deal is to secure it

explanation.surface: A nation obtaining something on the back of public fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a country, an island republic to the west of Britain.

clue.text: State in introduction to match: "team wearing green"

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter
the green word wears, that is surrounds, the team number

parts.note: eco is a prefix meaning environmentally friendly, green
XI is eleven, a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A sports team kitted out in green, as an opening match begins in some state.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a sovereign country, and state is used for a nation.

clue.text: Scottish Nationalist in street to press rejection of No

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them

indicators.note: rejection is read as throwing back, so the letters of no are turned round

explanation.surface: A Scottish independence campaigner out on the streets urging voters to reject the No camp.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the 2014 Scottish independence referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party and became First Minister of Scotland.

clue.text: See 3
Go Salmond in tatters! Alex gutted — no backing to enter race

indicators.note: to enter means these four letters go inside the rearranged name
something in tatters is torn to pieces, so the letters of go salmond are rearranged
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of Alex
backing means the word no is turned round

explanation.surface: A jeer at Alex Salmond, his campaign wrecked, gutted after the No vote in the independence race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in tatters' anagrams the name; 'gutted' and 'backing' make a four-letter insert. 'race' looks like a contest, like the referendum campaign, but it is the definition, a people.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers the English-speaking peoples descended from the Anglo-Saxons, treated as a race.

clue.text: Enter tentatively; one left, entering separately for medical course?

indicators.note: separately says the letter for left goes in at a different place from the first one, not alongside it
entering puts the letter for one inside the phrase for enter tentatively

parts.note: to pencil in is to write something down provisionally
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice on edging into a room, one person leaving, each arriving apart, about a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes after PEN and the L after PENICIL. The question mark marks the definition as a pun on a course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors prescribe a course of this antibiotic, so it is a medical course in the sense of treatment.

clue.text: Attack fool

definitions.meaning: to attack them, a two-word phrase
in British slang a ... is a silly or foolish person

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the phrasal verb go at, meaning assault; the other is slang for an idiot.

clue.text: See 27
"Vote Scotland" — detailed blog rewritten around English

indicators.note: around tells us the anagrammed letters go round the abbreviation for English
something rewritten is put down in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
de-tailed means the last letter is cut off the word blog

explanation.surface: A slogan urging Scots to vote, from a blog post that was revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' (de-tailed) removes the final letter; 'rewritten' anagrams the pool, and the English letter is set in after its first letter. 'Vote' reads as a command but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A second ballot is a further round of voting held when the first gives no outright winner.
